neighbours.label: the second occurrence of a word repeated for emphasis ('poor boy, poor fellow', 'despite X, despite Y')
fire: She looked at the ruined garden and whispered, 'Gone, all gone, gone forever.'
Through hunger, through cold, through every long winter, they kept the farm going.
He wanted more money, more power, more of everything he could reach.
It was never about the prize. Never. Never once did she care about it.
They walked for days, for weeks, for months across the empty plains.
Listen to me, please, please do not open that door tonight.
The answer is always the same: work, work and more work.
We will rebuild this town, brick by brick, street by street, home by home.
quiet: She looked at the ruined garden and whispered that everything was gone now.
Through the long winter they kept the farm going without much help.
He wanted a larger salary and a little more say in how things were run.
It was never about the prize; she did not care about it at all.
They walked for several months across the empty plains to the coast.
Listen to me carefully, and do not open that door tonight.
The answer is always the same: keep working until the job is done.
We will rebuild this town slowly, one careful step at a time.

notes: Card: top peaks are all on an immediately repeated word in rhetorical repetition: ' poor', ' kind', ' Can', ' despite', ' Only'.
